columns.title: FROBOT win it on Burrow's last drive
columns.author: sal
columns.teaser: Sour Grapes had the top score of the week until Joe Burrow's final drive Monday night. MR. FROBOT win by 2.9, take the 2 seed and stretch their streak to five. Hold Timers beat Bullish and keep climbing, and Jesus Christ College set a record nobody wants.
columns.caption: Joe Burrow, whose final drive Monday night was worth the game to MR. FROBOT
columns.html:
Sour Grapes did everything right this week. They set a near-perfect lineup, got 35.9 from their quarterback, and had the best score in the league with one game left to play. Then Joe Burrow got one last chance on Monday night, and it belonged to the team that always seems to get it.

FROBOT steal one

MR. FROBOT 136.3, Sour Grapes 133.4

Going into Monday night, Sour Grapes were sitting on 133.4. That was the top score of Week 11 at the time, and it wasn't a fluke. Dak Prescott put up 35.9, Chuba Hubbard 26.0, Bucky Irving 19.0 and the Ravens defense 17.0. Ken N. even got the lineup right. Their best possible score was 133.6, so he left two-tenths of a point on the table. C.J. Stroud's 20.5 sat on the bench again, but this time it didn't matter. Nobody beats 133.4 by accident.

FROBOT had already gotten 30.2 from CeeDee Lamb and 24.1 from Javonte Williams. What they still had was the Cincinnati stack, playing in Washington on Monday night: Joe Burrow, Tee Higgins, and Mike Gesicki, the $4 tight end they picked up for this week to cover for Kyren Williams and Harold Fannin Jr. on bye.

Here's how it went. Washington kicked a field goal with 2:26 left to go up 19-17. That was Burrow's last chance to win it for FROBOT, and he did it on back-to-back throws to the two FROBOT pass catchers on the field: 12 yards to Higgins, then 32 to Gesicki. The Bengals got to the Washington 38 with 51 seconds left. Burrow got sacked on third down, and Cincinnati settled for a 56-yard field goal and a 20-19 lead. That drive was worth about eight points to FROBOT: two to Higgins, four to Gesicki, close to two more for Burrow's passing yards. FROBOT won by 2.9.

Washington went 64 yards in four plays after that and kicked the winner. The Bengals lost the real game, 22-20. FROBOT won ours. Sour Grapes have one more thing to be sore about: their taxi-squad rookie, Antonio Williams, got the headlines for Washington's win the next morning. Taxi points don't count.

He can, and he does. I told you two weeks ago this was coming. FROBOT started 2-4. They've won five straight since, scored 717.3 over those five weeks, and lead the league in points with 1,465.7. They hold the Central on points over Hold Timers, they move up to the 2 seed, and their odds of a first-round bye went from 37% to 52%. That's six straight wins over Sour Grapes, too. Nobody in this league has won more since 2011, and this is what it looks like when they do it. They don't need your sympathy. They'd like your lunch money.

FROBOT's flex had a good week on the awards page, too. Javonte Williams moved onto the All-FBP 2nd Team. And Lamb is third in the MVP race with 252.2.

Sour Grapes get something out of it besides heartbreak. Prescott's 35.9 moved him up to the All-FBP 1st Team at quarterback. He has 237.7 starter points, and he passed Josh Allen to get there. At 3-8, Sour Grapes also slip from the 4th pick to the 5th.

Hold Timers stay hot, Bullish cool off

Hold Timers 101.4, Bullish on da Bears 87.5

Bullish came in 8-2 on a four-game winning streak. Hold Timers came in winners of three of their last four. Only one of those streaks survived.

Travis Kelce led Hold Timers with 25.4, the Bears defense put up 18.0, and Amon-Ra St. Brown added 14.7. It wasn't pretty, but it was enough, and that's four wins in five weeks for Hold Timers. They also left Jack Bech's 22.8 on the bench. Ronnie K. can live with that one.

Bullish can't say the same. Their bench had Mike Evans with 22.9 and Brock Purdy with 22.2. They started Pat Bryant (6.2) and Caleb Williams (14.3) instead. Their best possible lineup was 112.6, which beats 101.4. Ja'Marr Chase only gave them 8.1, though his season was good enough to move him up to the All-FBP 1st Team at flex. The Texans defense, their 18.0 top scorer this week, joined the 2nd Team.

Bullish are all but in, 100% in the computer's simulation, and they're still the 1 seed at 8-3. But the bye isn't the lock it looked like a week ago. Their bye odds dropped from 76% to 62%, and their chances at the 1 seed from 56% to 37%. They go to Hauk Tua next, and the computer makes them a 40% underdog. Bullish have scored 87.5 and 108.8 the last two weeks. That's cooling off.

Hold Timers went from 70% to 80% to make the playoffs, the biggest jump of the week, and they move up to the 4 seed at 7-4. Their win also moved their draft pick from 8th to 9th, which they'll happily take.

The rest of the card

Hauk Tua 98.4, Jesus Christ College 37.0

Start with the record. JCC's 37.0 is the lowest score in any FBP game since 2019. The old mark was 43.7, by Sour Grapes in 2022. Their starting quarterback, Jalon Daniels, scored 0.0. The Dolphins defense was their top scorer at 11.0, and nobody else reached 10. Their best possible lineup would have scored 50.9. Something to build on. At 2-9, they jump from the 5th pick to the 3rd, and they still own Bullish's first.

Jahmyr Gibbs put up 27.8 for Hauk Tua and took the MVP lead. He has 281.2 starter points, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 263.2, who didn't score this week. Gibbs is on pace for 365.5, which would break Christian McCaffrey's running back record of 354.1. That's two-thirds of the Triple Crown we wrote about last week, MVP and the All-FBP 1st Team, both in hand for now. The third part is the hard part. Hauk Tua are 6-5 and 7th, and their playoff odds slipped from 48% to 44% even with the win. No title, no crown.

Fully Cooked 105.5, Wholey Club 83.9

Patrick Mahomes 25.0 and Malik Nabers 18.5. Fully Cooked move up to the 3 seed and lead the West, and their odds of winning the division went from 54% to 70%. That's not great news for Wholey Club, who own Fully Cooked's first-round pick. It slides from 9th to 10th. Wholey Club still hold the 1st pick with their own.

The Fist of the Magi 122.1, Mailing It In 98.0

Ashton Jeanty 27.9, Jared Goff 20.4, and the Broncos defense 19.0, which put Denver back on the All-FBP 1st Team. Mailing It In played without Smith-Njigba and Bijan Robinson, who both put up zeros on the bench, and Bijan slipped to the All-FBP 2nd Team. The loss cost Mailing a lot. They fall from the 2 seed to the 5th, and their bye odds went from 25% to 9%. Son of Tinactin own Mailing's first, and it moves up from 11th to 8th. The Magi are 5-6 and drop from the 3rd pick to the 4th. Their playoff odds are 3%.

Thots & Players 94.9, Son of Tinactin 78.5

Tetairoa McMillan 19.1, Zay Flowers 16.4. Thots won, but they left Cam Ward's 22.2 and Baker Mayfield's 19.1 on the bench, and Josh Allen gave them 12.2. That cost Allen his All-FBP 1st Team spot. He's down to the 2nd Team behind Prescott, by 2.4 points. Thots hold the 6 seed on all-play wins. Son of Tinactin have lost three straight and stay at 2 in the draft.

Power rankings

MR. FROBOT are still No. 1, and the gap is growing.

Rank Team Last week
1 MR. FROBOT 1
2 Thots & Players 2
3 Fully Cooked 4
4 Mailing It In 3
5 Hold Timers 6
6 Bullish on da Bears 5
7 Hauk Tua 7
8 The Fist of the Magi 9
9 Wholey Club 8
10 Sour Grapes 10
11 Son of Tinactin 11
12 Jesus Christ College 12

The 1 seed is 6th in the power rankings. Bullish have the record. Five teams have the better rating.

Next week

Bullish go to Hauk Tua, and that's the game. Hauk Tua need it to get back in the playoff picture, and Bullish need it to keep the bye. FROBOT host Mailing It In as a 61% favorite. JCC get Hold Timers, which seems unfair.

And the trade deadline is Thursday, December 3, at 12 pm ET. Ten days. If you need a tight end, I hear FROBOT know where to find a cheap one.

columns.title: Hi, I'm Lainey. Let's talk about Jeremiah Smith.
columns.author: lainey
columns.teaser: The new draft and college column starts with the easiest pick in years, a 30,000-foot look at the 2027 class, how the top prospects did Saturday, and a draft order full of familiar faces.
columns.caption: Jeremiah Smith, Ohio State. Still the no-doubt 1.01.
columns.credit: Samantha Madar / The Columbus Dispatch / USA TODAY Network
columns.html:
Hi. I'm Lainey Pruitt, and this is the new college and draft column. Every Monday I'll tell you how the top 2027 prospects played that weekend and what it means for our rookie draft. I'll also keep Draft Home's "What to Know" current, and every week one prospect gets a closer look.

Some of you already know me from my other page. After college I started a subscription account to cover Son of Tinactin: news, lineup notes, injury updates, the occasional scarf. It got popular. Some of that was the football. Some of it wasn't, and I've made my peace with that. Either way, enough people were reading that the press box called and asked if I'd cover college and the draft for everybody. I said yes, as long as I could keep the scarf.

On the page I'm all business. Mostly.

Prospect of the week: Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State

We start at the top, because there's no real debate about the top.

Smith is a 6-4, 223-pound receiver who has produced since the week he got to Columbus. As a freshman on a national title team he caught 76 passes for 1,315 yards and 15 touchdowns. In 2025 it was 87 for 1,243 and 12, and a unanimous All-American nod. In September he torched Illinois for 12 catches, 217 yards and four touchdowns, all career highs. He owns the Big Ten's career records for receiving yards and touchdown catches.

Saturday at Nebraska he did it again: 6 catches, 165 yards, 2 touchdowns. The first was a 67-yarder on Ohio State's opening drive from freshman quarterback Luke Fahey. The second was a toe-drag 31-yarder late in the second quarter. That was his 17th touchdown catch of the year, tying Terry Glenn's Ohio State single-season record. It wasn't enough. Ohio State lost 31-28, its fourth loss and its first four-loss regular season since 2011.

That's the part I want you to notice. Ohio State is 7-4, the quarterback is a freshman, and Smith keeps putting up these lines anyway. Everybody in the building knows where the ball is going, and it doesn't matter. That's what a 1.01 looks like.

For FBP: whoever picks first takes him. Superflex doesn't change that. A quarterback can fill two spots for us next year, but Smith is the one rookie in this class you'd take over any of them in any format. The real question is what the team at No. 2 does, and I'll get to that.

Next: Michigan, Sat 12p ET FOX.

The 30,000-foot view

If you only read one section, read this one.

Quarterback is the story, and it's our story. FBP goes superflex in 2027, and this is a strong quarterback class arriving at the perfect moment. Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker, Miami's Darian Mensah, Notre Dame's CJ Carr, Oregon's Dante Moore and Texas's Arch Manning all sit in the top 14 of the board, with Ole Miss's Trinidad Chambliss right behind. Several could go in the NFL's first round. In a one-QB league you'd wait on all of them. In ours, expect two or three in the top eight, maybe ahead of a back or receiver you'd have loved last year.

Receiver is the deepest group. After Smith, Indiana's Charlie Becker leads the next tier, with Rutgers' KJ Duff, Texas's Cam Coleman and Indiana's Nick Marsh close behind. You'll find useful receivers well into the second round.

Running back is good at the top and shaky in the middle. Florida's Jadan Baugh is the best of the backs. Missouri's Ahmad Hardy, Ole Miss's Kewan Lacy and Georgia's Nate Frazier give it depth on paper, but Hardy and Lacy have both lost most of this season, so there are real questions heading into spring.

Tight end is thin. LSU's Trey'Dez Green and Oregon's Jamari Johnson are about it for early picks. If you need a tight end, don't plan on the draft.

How the board did this weekend

It was an ugly Saturday for the Big Ten's top teams, and a mixed one for our prospects.

Prospect Score Line
Smith, WR L 28-31 6 rec, 165 yds, 2 TD
Mestemaker, QB W 30-27 30/40, 294 yds, INT
Carr, QB W 24-3 19/29, 312 yds, TD, INT
Mensah, QB W 28-20 25/37, 241 yds, 2 INT
Manning, QB W 45-3 21/25, 287, 2 TD + rush TD
Baugh, RB W 34-27 19 car, 76 yds, TD
Becker, WR L 24-27 6 rec, 167 yds, TD
Coleman, WR W 45-3 1 rec, 16 yds
Hardy, RB W 28-14 3 car, 8 yds

Mestemaker was the gutsiest. He was a game-time decision with a strained right shoulder, didn't practice all week, and played the whole game anyway. Oklahoma State trailed 24-7 at the half and won in overtime.

Carr threw for 312 and the Irish defense did the rest. Notre Dame is 10-1 and a win at Syracuse should all but lock up a playoff spot.

Mensah had the worst stat line of the group: no touchdown passes for the first time this season and two picks, after throwing two all year. Miami's coaches say it was one of his best games anyway, and they have a point. He kept drives alive in a second half where Miami held the ball for 23 of 30 minutes, without his top receiver. He's still at 3,324 yards, 29 touchdowns and four interceptions on the year.

Manning went 21 of 25 in three quarters and sat the fourth. That's the version scouts were promised.

Baugh didn't have a big day, but he scored the go-ahead touchdown from 10 yards out with 2:18 left. He's at 981 yards and 16 rushing touchdowns, 19 yards from Florida's first back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons.

Becker was the best player on the field in a loss. A 74-yard touchdown on Indiana's first snap, 167 yards on seven targets, and his quarterback got benched anyway.

Coleman is playing through a shoulder injury and hasn't practiced. He caught the first pass of the game and was targeted once more.

Hardy is still being eased back in. He returned November 1 after missing most of the year with a leg injury, and he's had 14 carries since.

Out for the year: Ole Miss's Kewan Lacy (shoulder) and Rutgers' KJ Duff (high ankle surgery). Duff is expected to enter the draft. Lacy has a year of eligibility left and hasn't said.

The FBP draft order

Picks 1 through 6 go to the non-playoff teams, worst potential points first. Picks 7 through 12 follow the playoffs, so for now they're projected by seed. Here's where it stands after Week 11.

Pick Team Last week
1 Wholey Club 1
2 Son of Tinactin 2
3 Jesus Christ College 5
4 The Fist of the Magi 3
5 Sour Grapes 4
6 Hauk Tua 6
7 Thots & Players 7
8 Mailing It In* 11
9 Hold Timers 8
10 Fully Cooked* 9
11 MR. FROBOT 10
12 Bullish on da Bears* 12

*Traded: Son of Tinactin owns Mailing It In's pick, Wholey Club owns Fully Cooked's, and Jesus Christ College owns Bullish on da Bears'.

The race for 1.01 is tight. Wholey Club has 1,224.9 potential points, Son of Tinactin 1,246.8 and Jesus Christ College 1,271.0. That's 21.9 points between the top two and another 24.2 to third, which is one big week either way. The Fist of the Magi (1,330.9) and Sour Grapes (1,352.9) are further back. Three weeks are left, so all three of those picks are still in play, and the winner gets Smith.

JCC is the mover, from fifth to third. Remember, the order runs on potential points, not actual points, so a bad lineup doesn't help you here. A bad roster does. JCC scored a record-low 37.0 last week, and their best possible lineup would only have scored 50.9. The Fist of the Magi's best possible lineup scored 143.6, which is why they slid back to fourth.

Pick 6 is a playoff question. Hauk Tua is the best team outside the field and has about a 44 percent chance to get in. If they make it, someone else becomes the sixth pick. The Fist of the Magi (2.7 percent) and Wholey Club (0.4 percent) are hanging on by a thread.

Some teams are double-dipping. Wholey Club has 1 and 10. Son of Tinactin has 2 and 8. JCC has 3 and 12. In a superflex year with this many quarterbacks, two first-rounders is a real advantage. If you're picking 2 or 3, you can take the best quarterback on the board and still get a shot at Becker or Baugh with your second pick.

All three of those teams play in the East. The fourth East team, Bullish on da Bears, has no first at all. Their pick belongs to JCC. Bullish leads the division now, but the other three are lining up for next year.

Familiar faces

Here's the part some of you won't love. All five teams in the top five right now have picked in the top five before. These teams know the neighborhood.

  • Son of Tinactin: 2nd in 2021 (Javonte Williams), 1st in 2024 (Marvin Harrison Jr.), 3rd in 2025 (TreVeyon Henderson), 3rd in 2026 (Carnell Tate). That's four top-three picks in six drafts. I'm not going to comment on that.
  • Jesus Christ College: 4th in 2021 (Trey Sermon), 2nd in 2022 (Kenneth Walker III), 1st in 2026 (Jeremiyah Love). In the six drafts on the books, no team has picked 1.01 two years running. They're two spots away.
  • The Fist of the Magi: 1st in 2021 (Najee Harris), 1st in 2025 (Ashton Jeanty), 5th in 2026 (Jordyn Tyson). The only team with two 1.01s.
  • Sour Grapes: 3rd in 2023 (Zach Charbonnet), 4th in 2024 (Xavier Worthy), 2nd in 2026 (Makai Lemon).
  • Wholey Club: 4th in 2022 (Garrett Wilson), 2nd in 2025 (Omarion Hampton). They've never had the first pick. They're holding it right now.

Next Monday

Rivalry week. Smith gets Michigan, Manning and Coleman go to College Station on Friday night, and Baugh needs 19 yards in Tallahassee. I'll be watching all of it. If you're picking in the top five, you should be too. You've probably done this before.

How to watch: Baugh at Florida State, Fri 3:30p ET ABC. Manning and Coleman at Texas A&M, Fri 7:30p ET ABC. Smith vs Michigan, Sat 12p ET FOX. Carr at Syracuse, Sat 12p ET ABC. Mensah vs Boston College, Sat 12p ET ESPN. Mestemaker vs Kansas, Sat 6:15p ET ESPN2. Becker vs Purdue, Sat 7p ET FS1.

See you next Monday.

Lainey

columns.title: Gibbs, Smith-Njigba and the rarest thing in this league
columns.author: sal
columns.teaser: Win MVP, make the All-FBP team and lift the trophy, all in one season. It's been done twice. Jahmyr Gibbs and Jaxon Smith-Njigba are both on pace for the best season this league has ever seen, and only one of them can get all three.
columns.caption: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Mailing It In's receiver and the FBP scoring leader
columns.html:
In eight seasons, 96 teams have chased a Footballpalooza title, and plenty of players have put up monster years along the way. Only two have done all three things a player can do in one season: win MVP, make the All-FBP team and win the championship.

The site calls it the Triple Crown now. You'll find it on the Awards page, and on the Player Pages of the two men who own it.

This year, two more players are in the hunt, and both are chasing history while they're at it.

The two who did it

Cooper Kupp, 2021, Mailing It In. Kupp was making $25 that year and scored 335.4 points in 13 starts, 25.8 a start. It's still the best season a receiver has ever had in this league, and the second-best by anybody. Mailing It In earned a first-round bye, and Kupp picked up where he left off: 21.3 in a 162.9-95.1 semifinal rout of FROBOT, then 21.5 in the title game, a 140.2-111.2 win over Thots & Players. The season wasn't close and neither was the final.

Tyreek Hill, 2023, MR. FROBOT. Hill went for 322.7 in 13 starts at $31 and took MVP. FROBOT had a first-round bye, then Hill put up 18.9 in a 123.2-95.1 semifinal win over Thots & Players and 13.6 in the title game, where FROBOT got past Fist of the Magi 135.3-126.6. Not his biggest weeks, but the trophy doesn't ask.

Both seasons sit on the All-Time FBP Team today.

The one that got away, five times

Here's what makes the crown so hard. Every MVP this league has crowned also made the All-FBP 1st Team. That part comes with the territory. The title is what keeps slipping:

  • Christian McCaffrey, 2019, Fist of the Magi: 354.1 points, the best season ever. No title.
  • Patrick Mahomes, 2020, Bullish on da Bears: MVP, no title.
  • Jalen Hurts, 2022, MR. FROBOT: the best quarterback season ever. No title.
  • Lamar Jackson, 2024, Wholey Club: MVP, no title.
  • McCaffrey again, 2025, Wholey Club: MVP, no title.

Five MVPs, five teams that came up short in December. One great player can carry you to the playoffs. He can't play all eight spots.

Gibbs vs. Smith-Njigba

Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Mailing It In. 263.2 points in 10 starts, 26.3 a start. He leads the league and he's started every week. He's on bye today, then has three games left. At his pace he finishes around 342. That would pass Kupp's 335.4 for the best receiver season in league history, for the same franchise that rode Kupp to the crown.

Jahmyr Gibbs, Hauk Tua. 253.4 points in 9 starts, 28.2 a start, the best rate of anyone in the league. He had his bye in week 6, so he has four games left, starting today against JCC. At his pace he finishes around 366. That would be the best season this league has ever seen, past McCaffrey's 354.1 from 2019.

The MVP goes to the top scorer, and right now it's 9.8 points between them. With Smith-Njigba sitting today, Gibbs could take the lead by tonight. Josh Allen is third at 223.1, close enough to keep an eye on but nobody's betting that way. Both are on the current All-FBP 1st Team, and barring injury, they'll stay there.

So it comes down to the trophy.

The catch

Mailing It In is 6-3-1 with a 91% shot at the playoffs. That's the good news. The schedule is the bad news: FROBOT, Thots & Players and Fully Cooked to close, all of them toss-ups on paper. They're also the defending champions, and Kevin M. has won this thing before with a Triple Crown receiver. He knows exactly what it looks like.

Hauk Tua is 5-5, and its playoff odds are 48%, a coin flip. Gibbs has done everything asked of him, and Hauk Tua still sits in the middle of the pack. The next two weeks are JCC, then Bullish on da Bears. I'll leave it there.

That's the twist. The player having the best season in league history might not even make the playoffs. The one with the cleaner path still has to get through three tough weeks, then win every playoff game he plays.

What's at stake

If Smith-Njigba pulls it off, Mailing It In becomes the first franchise with two Triple Crowns. If Gibbs does it, he does it with the best season this league has ever recorded, on a team that was .500 in late November.

Two players have done it in eight years. By January, one of these two could be the third. Or, like five MVPs before them, they find out the trophy was the hard part.

columns.title: Two weeks to the deadline: how to read the Trading Floor
columns.author: devin
columns.teaser: The Trading Floor is out of Beta and into League Now, and the trade block now follows players around the site. A guide to every tab, and how the league looks from the outside two weeks before the Dec 3 deadline.
columns.caption: Bucky Irving, on Sour Grapes' trade block since Oct 23
columns.html:
The trade deadline is Thursday, Dec 3 at 12 PM ET. That's two weeks from today, and two more weeks of games, 11 and 12, before in-season trading closes.

The Trading Floor is out of Beta. It now lives in League Now: open the ▾ beside League Now and it's right under Analytics. It doesn't tell anyone what to do. It's a view of the league from the outside, built from the same public data for everyone: who's on the block, which players fit the usual reasons to move, where each roster is deep or thin, and what everything is worth. Every owner sees exactly the same page.

Here's how each part works, and what it shows as of Wednesday night's data refresh.

Trade Value, first

Everything on the Trading Floor leads with one number, Trade Value. It runs from 1 to 9,999 and tries to answer a simple question: what is this player worth in a trade between FBP owners?

It starts with talent and then adjusts for the contract.

  • Talent leads. It's a mix of how a player is producing right now and his dynasty outlook. This season counts double, because the playoff run is what a contender is buying. Stars are weighted up, so two good players don't add up to one great one.
  • The contract adjusts it, by at most about a third either way. That covers how many seasons you control him and how his salary compares with what he'd go for at the auction. A cheap deal helps. A big salary or a short deal hurts.
  • A year nobody would pay ends the deal. If a future salary runs past what a player would fetch at auction, Trade Value assumes he gets let go that year. A three-year deal with a bad last year counts as two.

That's why a star on a fair contract stays well above a good player on a cheap one. You don't trade a great player for a lesser one just because of money. The model doesn't either.

One more thing: Trade Value isn't the FBP OVR. The OVR next to each name is the player rating, with nothing about money in it. Trade Value is the same player with his contract counted.

The Value Chart

The Value Chart puts all of this on one page. Value levels run down the left in 250-point bands, with a column for each position and one for rookie picks. Players in the same row are worth about the same.

Here's one row as an example. Between 6,501 and 6,750 you'll find Puka Nacua (6,513), Tetairoa McMillan (6,552), Christian Watson (6,669) and Wholey Club's 2027 1st, currently projected at 1.01, at 6,745. That doesn't mean anyone would make any of those swaps. It only means the model puts them at about the same level.

The top of the chart is Jaxon Smith-Njigba, alone at 9,999.

On the Block

This tab reads MFL's Trade Bait list. Any owner can add players to it from his team page in MFL, and it shows up here on the next refresh. Four teams have someone on it right now:

  • Thots & Players: Cam Ward, David Montgomery and Jonathan Taylor, on the list since Aug 29
  • Fully Cooked: Nico Collins and Jadarian Price
  • Sour Grapes: Bucky Irving
  • Jesus Christ College: Tyler Allgeier, Jaylen Waddle and Juwan Johnson, looking for cash and picks

Spotting the block around the site

The trade block isn't a secret anymore. Any player on Trade Bait now carries a gold TRADE chip beside his name wherever he shows up: the Scoreboard and Players pages, Rosters, My Team, his Player Page, Stats, Rankings and the Value Chart. Take a player off Trade Bait in MFL and the chip goes away on the next refresh.

Targets

Targets doesn't list every player on every team out of the race. It lists sell candidates: players on teams outside a playoff spot who fit one of the usual reasons a player gets moved instead of carried into next season. It looks for four:

  • Expiring: his contract ends after this season
  • Cost: his 2027 salary is more than he'd go for at the auction
  • Sell high: he's producing well above his long-term value
  • Peak age: he's at or past his position's peak while his Trade Value is still high

There are 36 sell candidates this week. The top five by Trade Value:

Player Team Trade Value Contract Why
Christian Watson, WR Hauk Tua 6,669 $4, $10 in 2027 Sell high, 18.4 ppg
Bucky Irving, RB Sour Grapes 5,311 $14, expiring Expiring, sell high
Chuba Hubbard, RB Sour Grapes 4,726 $15, $18 in 2027 Sell high, 18.1 ppg
DeVonta Smith, WR Jesus Christ College 4,427 $16, $22 in 2027 Age 28, the WR peak
Davante Adams, WR The Fist of the Magi 3,328 $15, $18 in 2027 Sell high, 17.0 ppg

Two notes on that table. First, Targets is a snapshot. Hauk Tua are 5-5 with 48.1% playoff odds, and Watson shows up only because they're outside a playoff spot this week. A win could take them off the list entirely.

Second, here's what the "cost" reason looks like in practice. Derrick Henry is averaging 16.1 a game for The Fist of the Magi. He's $47 next year, and the model estimates he'd go for about $24 at the auction.

Thinking outside the box

Targets leaves playoff teams out, except here. This section lists 27 players on playoff teams who fit one of three roster or money reasons: more good players at his position than the team will start in 2027, a third keeper-worthy QB, or a 2027 keeper bill over budget.

The top of this list is mostly about money. Matthew Golden (7,311) and Tetairoa McMillan (6,552) lead it, both from Thots & Players, whose 2027 keeper bill is the furthest over budget in the league. More on that below.

Teams

The Teams tab shows where needs and surpluses line up. Each team's card shows its playoff odds, an outlook (Contending at 75% or better, In the mix from 25% to 75%, Building under 25%), and its depth: how many players rated 80 or better it has at each position. One more than the lineup needs is deep. Fewer is thin.

Then it lines up needs with surpluses. A team that's thin somewhere is listed with the teams that are deep there. Two playoff teams are only listed together when it runs both ways, each deep where the other is thin.

This week there's exactly one pair of playoff teams like that:

  • Bullish on da Bears (8-2, 99.9%) are thin at RB, with one back rated 80+, and deep at QB and WR.
  • Mailing It In (6-3-1, 91.2%) are thin at QB, with none rated 80+, and deep at RB.

On paper, each is deep where the other is thin. That's as far as the tab goes.

Elsewhere, three Building teams are thin at RB: Wholey Club, Son of Tinactin and Jesus Christ College. Sour Grapes are thin at TE, and the only team deep there is Thots & Players.

Each card also shows the 2027 money: payroll, what it would cost to keep everyone worth keeping, and the budget after auction cash traded. Eight of the twelve teams would be over. Thots & Players are furthest over: $316 to keep 13 players against a $192 budget, $124 over.

Keeper crunches

The Keeper crunches list, back on Targets, covers the same ground. It flags teams that can't keep everyone worth keeping, either by the $200 cap or by the 2027 rule of two veteran QBs. There are 17 crunches across the league this week: eight on the cap and nine on the QB limit.

MR. FROBOT have the most quarterbacks against the limit, five under contract for 2027: Joe Burrow, Jalen Hurts, Tyler Shough, Ty Simpson and Mac Jones. Superflex makes that a deep room, and the limit means some of it can't be kept.

Trade Habits and History

The last two tabs look back. History has every MFL trade since 2019, 147 of them, with auction cash from the commissioner's trade log. Filter by season, team or type (with picks, with cash, players only, picks only), and open "How it played out" to follow each side's points forward. That includes players taken with traded picks, and anything flipped later.

Trade Habits counts the same history by team. It's plain counts, and there's no right number. Some teams trade often: Thots & Players have made 46 trades, Bullish 44 and Son of Tinactin 43, and Thots and Son of Tinactin have traded with each other 12 times. Bullish make 33 of their 44 during the season. Others trade less often: Sour Grapes have made 4 trades since 2019, all during the season.

What it all adds up to

Eight trades so far in the 2026 league year, four of them in one week in October. Two weeks left. From the outside, the Floor shows 36 sell candidates, one mirrored pair of playoff teams, and 17 keeper crunches spread across nine teams. What anyone does with that is up to them.

Data through Wednesday night's refresh: rosters, contracts, picks, trades and Trade Bait from MFL; playoff odds from League Now; auction cash in trades from the commissioner's trade log. Trade Value is a model, and it's still being refined. Every list here describes rosters from the outside. None of it is a verdict on a team or a recommendation to anyone.

columns.title: Mailing It In find a defense. They're still missing two stars.
columns.author: sal
columns.teaser: Mailing It In patched the hole at defense on waivers, but Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Bijan Robinson are still on bye. Hold Timers visit Bullish with the most playoff odds on the line.
columns.caption: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, 263.2 points and the week off
columns.html:
Six NFL teams are off this week: Atlanta, Cleveland, Green Bay, the Rams, New England and Seattle. No FBP team loses more points to it than Mailing It In, the team in first place in the West.

A word on the win chances below. They come from the site's computer, which knows how well your team has played. It doesn't know who's on bye.

Mailing It In (6-3-1) at The Fist of the Magi (4-6)

The computer likes Mailing at 65%. It hasn't looked at the roster. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the MVP leader, is off. So is Bijan Robinson. That's 460.9 points between them. Mailing also carry two defenses, Green Bay and Cleveland, and both are on bye.

Wednesday's waivers fixed part of that. Mailing claimed the Chargers defense, projected for 12.3, and receiver Elic Ayomanor, projected for 10.0. Their best lineup now comes to 110.4. The Magi's best is 109.2. Yes, those Magi, losers of five straight at 69.6 a game over the last three.

Fully Cooked had the same problem, with New England as their only defense. They went and got the Jets.

Hold Timers (6-4) at Bullish on da Bears (8-2)

No game moves more playoff odds. Hold Timers hold the 5 seed at 70%, and they go to 82% with a win or 52% with a loss. Bullish are playing for the bye: 95% with a win, 63% with a loss.

The computer has the 1 seed as a 42% underdog in its own building. It made them an underdog in Week 9 too, and Bullish won by 35.5. My old man would have had a word for that computer. I'll leave it there.

The projections have it 121.7 to 119.7, Hold Timers. Bullish have won four straight and lead the series 6-3, but Brock Bowers is questionable with an ankle. Hold Timers lose Drake London and Blake Corum to byes. Their best flex is Xavier Hutchinson, claimed Wednesday and projected for 9.1, while Emmett Johnson sits on the taxi squad at 11.2. I asked Tuesday if Ronnie K. calls him up. A game this close makes it a harder question.

Around the league

Hauk Tua (5-5) at Jesus Christ College (2-8). Hauk Tua are the first team out: 55% with a win, 28% with a loss. Drake Maye is off, so it's Kirk Cousins. JCC have it worse. They cut Deshaun Watson on Wednesday, a week after claiming him. Malik Willis and Jaxson Dart are on IR, and the best quarterback left is Cade Klubnik, projected for 4.6.

Thots & Players (5-5) at Son of Tinactin (3-6-1). Thots project for 130.8 and have an 82% chance. Tinactin play without Jordan Love. They also own Mailing's first-round pick, so they'll have an eye on the Magi game.

Fully Cooked (6-4) at Wholey Club (5-5). Cooked are an 84% favorite with the week's top projection, 131.9, though that counts on Kenneth Walker III, who's questionable with a groin injury. Wholey have the fewest points in the league, two straight wins and a 5-2 lead in this series. They also own Cooked's first-round pick, and that pick gets better if Cooked slide.

Sour Grapes (3-7) at MR. FROBOT (6-4). FROBOT have won four straight and five in a row in this series, and they're a 79% favorite. Kyren Williams and Harold Fannin Jr. are on bye, so they spent $4 on Mike Gesicki to play tight end.

One more thing. The trade deadline is Thursday, December 3, at 12 pm ET. That's two Sundays from now. Weeks like this one show you how thin you are, and Jonathan Taylor, Nico Collins and Bucky Irving are all sitting on the trading block.

See you after the games. Bring the coffee.

columns.title: Hold Timers win the Detroit civil war, and Fully Cooked lose it at the podium
columns.author: sal
columns.teaser: Hold Timers put up the week's top score and climb back into the 5 seed past Hauk Tua. Thots & Players sweep Fully Cooked by less than a point behind Christian McCaffrey's 46.3. Then Collin D. took the podium.
columns.caption: Christian McCaffrey, Thots & Players' running back and the Week 10 Player of the Week
columns.html:
Two games mattered this week, and both of them delivered. One was the best game on the card. The other ended with a 0.9-point margin, a sweep, and the best press conference this league has seen in years. I've been doing this sixteen years. I took notes.

Hold Timers win the Detroit civil war

Hold Timers 148.8, Hauk Tua 131.7

I said this was the game of the week, and it was. It was the highest-scoring game of Week 10 at 280.5 combined, and Hold Timers' 148.8 was the top score in the league.

Detroit split it. Jahmyr Gibbs put up 44.2 for Hauk Tua, the second-best game of the week by anyone. Amon-Ra St. Brown played through the rib injury and gave Hold Timers 25.8. Gibbs won that duel by 18.4. Hold Timers won the game by 17.1, because Hold Timers had help. Chase Brown 28.3, Trevor Lawrence 26.8 with Bo Nix on bye, and Blake Corum 20.9 filling in for D'Andre Swift. They lost three starters to byes and still put up the best score in the league.

Hauk Tua will look at the bench and wince. Drake Maye gave them 3.0. Kirk Cousins scored 15.4 sitting next to Quinshon Judkins' 16.1. Hauk Tua's best possible lineup would have scored 153.5. That wins this game.

This was the game that decided which of these two holds a playoff spot going into Week 11, and the computer reacted about the way I said it would. Hold Timers went from 49% to 70% to make the playoffs. Hauk Tua went from 67% to 48%. Hold Timers are back in the 5 seed at 6-4. Hauk Tua are 5-5 and the first team out. Hauk Tua still lead the series, 7-5, but this was the one that counted. FROBOT probably take the Central. These two are probably fighting over one spot, and right now Hold Timers have it.

Thots sweep, and Collin takes the podium

Thots & Players 137.4, Fully Cooked 136.5

Christian McCaffrey scored 46.3. That's the top score in the league this season, by anyone, starting or sitting. It made him Player of the Week, and it was the difference in a game decided by 0.9 points. Josh Allen added 22.3 and the Vikings defense 23.0. Thots also set the perfect lineup: 137.4 scored, 137.4 possible.

Fully Cooked did plenty. Patrick Mahomes went for 35.4, Nico Collins 24.4, James Cook 21.7. But they left Samaje Perine's 13.9 on the bench and started Malik Nabers, who gave them 7.4. Their best possible lineup was 143.0. Without Puka Nacua, who's on IR, there wasn't much room for error.

If this felt familiar, it should. In Week 4 Fully Cooked scored 153.7, still their best week of the season, and lost to Thots 157.7 to 153.7. Tetairoa McMillan put up 45.2 in that one, which was the comeback. Here's the number that matters for what came next. There have been exactly two 45-point games in this league this season. McMillan's 45.2 and McCaffrey's 46.3. Both came for Thots. Both came against Fully Cooked.

That's a sweep for Thots, their fifth straight win in the series, and a 10-4 lead in it since 2019. Fully Cooked fell from the 2 seed to the 4 and lost first place in the West. Their odds of a bye went from 61% to 40%.

Then came the handshake line. Paul M. says Collin D. said something there I won't print. Then Collin got to the podium.

"Needing miracles is never a good thing," he said about Thots' big games against him. He called McMillan and McCaffrey "a bum and a white guy." And he went on: "Having guys go nuclear twice in a season... something that could possibly never ever happen again in their entire careers against me and have that be why he won is legit rare air of luck." And he finished with this: "It's insane. He's needed 2 all-time career games in both our matchups. It's as simple as that."

I checked his numbers, because that's the job. He's half right. McMillan's 45.2 is the best game of his FBP career by more than 12 points. McCaffrey's 46.3 isn't even his best. He put up 48.7 in Week 4 of 2023.

On going nuclear, the site's Heat Check counts every starter who hits the nuclear line for his position. Fully Cooked's starters have gone nuclear eight times this season, tied for third-most in the league. Kenneth Walker III has done it three times by himself, Nacua twice. Thots' starters have done it five times. And Thots' opponents have gone nuclear against them 10 times, tied for the most in the league. One of them was Mahomes on Sunday. Big games happen to everybody. Fully Cooked just ran into two in the same building.

Paul M. had his own podium. "He thinks it's lucky Christian McCaffrey has the high score for the week," he said. "While he's over there getting 35 points from Patrick (expletive) Mahomes on a $2 contract." He's right about that one. Mahomes cost $2 at the auction and he's second for Best Value. Paul M. kept going: "Talk about luck, he stumbled (expletive) first into a 4th round Puka Nacua." That one checks out too. Nacua was pick 4.04 in 2023. Paul M. closed with: "I'm riding high right now. I just swept a division rival and I'm in his head rent free."

Thots are the 6 seed. Fully Cooked are the 4. A playoff meeting isn't out of the question. I'd like a seat for that one.

The rest of the card

MR. FROBOT 136.7, The Fist of the Magi 80.9

Joe Burrow 33.2, Parker Washington 28.7, CeeDee Lamb 20.2. FROBOT also left Cam Skattebo's 27.2 on the bench and won by 55.8 anyway. That's four straight wins. They still lead the Central at 6-4 over Hold Timers on points, and their odds of winning the division went from 60% to 66%. The Magi have lost five straight and their playoff odds are down to 2%. The good news for them is in the draft: they move from the 4th pick to the 3rd.

Mailing It In 138.7, Sour Grapes 112.2

Jaxon Smith-Njigba 31.1, Deebo Samuel 28.0. Mailing It In end a two-game skid and take first in the West and the 2 seed from Fully Cooked. Their playoff odds went from 85% to 91%. Sour Grapes got 34.4 from Dak Prescott and 34.2 from Chuba Hubbard and still lost by 26.5. C.J. Stroud put up 20.4 on the bench again. Sour Grapes slide from 3rd to 4th in the draft order.

Wholey Club 102.8, Son of Tinactin 83.0

Stefon Diggs 20.3, Matthew Stafford 19.8. In the Draft Bowl, losing is the point, and Son of Tinactin managed it. It didn't help them much. The draft order runs on potential points, not wins, and Tinactin's lineup could have scored 137.4, with George Pickens' 43.5 sitting on the bench. That's the third-best score by anyone in the league this week. Wholey Club's best possible lineup was 119.4. So Wholey Club won the game and still gained in the race for the top pick. Their edge for the 1.01 grew from 15.9 potential points to 33.9. Tinactin stay at 2.

Bullish on da Bears 108.8, Jesus Christ College 89.3

Ja'Marr Chase 34.1, Brock Purdy 31.7. Bullish are 8-2 with four straight wins, and their bye odds went from 66% to 76%. JCC are 2-8 and stay at 5 in the draft. They also own Bullish's first, which is still projected 12th.

The playoff picture

Seed Team Record Last week
1 Bullish on da Bears 8-2 1
2 Mailing It In 6-3-1 4
3 MR. FROBOT 6-4 3
4 Fully Cooked 6-4 2
5 Hold Timers 6-4 out
6 Thots & Players 5-5 6

Rising: Hold Timers jumped from 49% to 70%, the biggest move of the week. Mailing It In went from 85% to 91% and took the 2 seed. Thots went from 88% to 92%.

Falling: Hauk Tua dropped from 67% to 48% and out of the picture. Fully Cooked are still at 98% to make it, but they lost the West lead and two seeds. The Magi went from 14% to 2%.

Hauk Tua sit 7th, and they get both reports this week since they're right on the bubble. In the playoff race they're 5-5, tied with Thots and a game behind Hold Timers. In the draft race they jump from the 8th pick to the 6th. Next up is JCC.

The draft order

Picks 1-6 go to the non-playoff teams in order of lowest potential points. Picks 7-12 are projected by seed.

2 Son of Tinactin 2
3 The Fist of the Magi 4
4 Sour Grapes 3

10 MR. FROBOT 10
11 Mailing It In * 9
12 Bullish on da Bears * 12

* Traded picks: Wholey Club own Fully Cooked's, Son of Tinactin own Mailing It In's, and Jesus Christ College own Bullish's.

Rising: The Magi move up to 3. Hauk Tua jump from 8 to 6. Wholey Club also come out ahead: Fully Cooked's loss moves their pick from 11th to 9th, and Wholey Club own it.

Falling: Hold Timers' win moved them back into a playoff seed and out of the top six. They go from 6 to 8. Son of Tinactin's extra first, Mailing's, slides from 9th to 11th with Mailing in the 2 seed.

Awards watch

On a record pace. Smith-Njigba leads the MVP race with 263.2 points, and the site has him on pace for 342.1. The single-season record for a wide receiver is Cooper Kupp's 335.4 from 2021. Gibbs is second in the MVP race with 253.4 and on pace for 366.2. The running back record is 354.1, set in 2019 by Christian McCaffrey. So the man who just had the best game of the season is also the one whose record Gibbs is chasing.

All-FBP, rising: McCaffrey's 46.3 moved him onto the first team at running back. The Vikings defense (Thots) took over the first-team defense spot from Denver. James Cook III (Fully Cooked) joined the second team, and Amon-Ra St. Brown is back on it.

All-FBP, falling: McCaffrey's jump bumped Kenneth Walker III to the second team. Nacua (IR) and Javonte Williams dropped off the list.

Where's Burrow? People keep asking me why Joe Cool isn't on an All-FBP team. Burrow has 232.4 points this season, the most of any quarterback in the league. But All-FBP counts starter points, and Sean M. didn't start him in Weeks 2 through 4. Jalen Hurts and Tyler Shough got those starts while Burrow put up 62.5 points on the bench. Add the Week 6 bye and Burrow has 169.9 starter points. Dak Prescott holds the second-team spot with 201.8. Burrow's closing fast, though. He's averaged 32.8 over his last four starts. At that rate he catches Prescott in two or three weeks.

Introducing the All-FBP Rookie Team. It's new this year. The Rookie Team counts every point a rookie scores, whether he's starting, on the bench or on the taxi squad. Plenty of good rookies spend the season on taxi on purpose to keep them cheap, and the regular All-FBP teams never see them. You'll know them on the site by the green ring on their photos. Rookie of the Year now counts the same way.

This year's team: Fernando Mendoza at QB, Emmett Johnson and Seth McGowan at RB, Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion at WR, Kenyon Sadiq at TE and Carnell Tate at flex. Son of Tinactin have three of the seven. Hold Timers have two.

A new Rookie of the Year leader. Emmett Johnson scored 35.1 this week and went from fourth to first. He has 112.0 points, ahead of Boston's 108.2. Johnson was the 2.06 pick, he makes $3, and every one of those points came on Hold Timers' taxi squad. That raises a question for Ronnie K. Does he get called up? Hold Timers just won a playoff fight with a running back committee. Promoting Johnson now gets them a back who's scored 73.5 over the last three weeks. The cost is in the rulebook: his salary escalators start early and he gives up the sixth-year option. I wouldn't want to make that call.

Manager of the Year. It's not just record. The site combines a few different measures into one score to find the team that's been run the best. Bullish lead, and Hold Timers moved up from third to second. Mailing It In joined the top three, and Fully Cooked dropped out.

Next week

Hold Timers host Bullish, and the computer gives them a 58% chance. Hauk Tua get JCC. Thots get Son of Tinactin. Fully Cooked get Wholey Club, who own their first-round pick and would very much like Fully Cooked to keep winning.

One more thing. The trade deadline is Thursday, December 3, at 12 pm ET. If your team needs something for the stretch, you're running out of Thursdays. Get your calls in. Somebody please call Collin.

columns.title: A Detroit civil war in the Central
columns.author: sal
columns.teaser: Hold Timers visit Hauk Tua with a 78-point playoff swing on the line and three starters on bye, Thots try to stop a three-game slide against the team they always beat, and the two teams fighting over the 1.01 play each other.
columns.caption: Amon-Ra St. Brown (14) and Jahmyr Gibbs (0), Lions teammates on opposite sides of Sunday's game of the week
columns.html:
Three teams are 5-4 in the Central. Only one of them is in first, and the other two play each other on Sunday. That's the game. Everything else on this week's card is a sideshow, and one of those sideshows is the West lead.

Win chances come from the site's computer, which plays out the rest of the season 20,000 times. Series records count every meeting since 2019, playoffs included.

Hold Timers (5-4) at Hauk Tua (5-4) — game of the week

Hauk Tua hold the 5 seed. Hold Timers are the first team out. Hold Timers' playoff odds go from 49% to 70% with a win or 30% with a loss; Hauk Tua's go from 67% to 84% or 47%. That's 77.6 points of playoff odds riding on one division game. No other game this week moves more than 24.5.

The computer has Hauk Tua a 53% favorite, and the projections have them up 121.0 to 114.0. Blame the bye list: Hold Timers lose D'Andre Swift, Bo Nix and the Bears defense. Hauk Tua only lose Colston Loveland.

Then there's Detroit. Hauk Tua's best player is Jahmyr Gibbs, with 209.2 points, the most by any running back in the league. Hold Timers' best player is his teammate Amon-Ra St. Brown, at 159.4, and he's questionable with a rib injury. Whatever the Lions do on Sunday shows up on both sides of this box score. Hauk Tua have worries too: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle, foot) didn't practice Wednesday, and the Vikings won't commit to Kirk Cousins as their starter after trading for him.

Hauk Tua have the form, two straight wins and 131.6 a game over their last three, and the history, 7-4 in the series with the last two. Hold Timers have the 2019 semifinal, the only playoff meeting, which they won 153.0 to 143.4. That's not much, but it's something.

Thots & Players (4-5) at Fully Cooked (6-3)

Fully Cooked lead the West. Thots have lost three straight. And the projections still have Thots ahead, 129.5 to 128.9. The computer calls it 52-48 for Cooked.

Cooked are at 99% to make the playoffs either way. The bye is what's at stake: 78% with a win, 43% with a loss. A win also gets them to 7-3, one victory from their first winning season since the league went PPR. Thots are at 88%, 82% with a loss, and they're too good a team (third in points, 65-34 all-play) to stay on a slide like this.

The trouble for Cooked is the series. Thots lead it 9-4 and have won four straight, including 157.7 to 153.7 in Week 4. And Cooked play this one without Puka Nacua, who's out until mid-December with a knee injury. Thots are missing David Montgomery (questionable) and Rome Odunze (bye), but they have Josh Allen, projected for 26.8.

Around the league

The Fist of the Magi (4-5) at MR. FROBOT (5-4). FROBOT are a 69% favorite, have won three straight and lead the league in points. The Magi have lost four straight and averaged 67.3 over their last three, the lowest in the league by almost nine points. FROBOT lead the series 12-3, but the Magi won both meetings last year.

Mailing It In (5-3-1) at Sour Grapes (3-6). The champs have lost two straight and are a 71% favorite. Sour Grapes just knocked off Hold Timers and lead the series 6-5.

Son of Tinactin (3-5-1) at Wholey Club (4-5). Call it the Draft Bowl. These two are sitting on the 1.01 and 1.02. The draft order runs on potential points, not wins, so whichever team has the bigger week slides toward 1.02, win or lose.

Bullish on da Bears (7-2) at Jesus Christ College (2-7). Bullish are a 63% favorite and playing for the bye: 79% with a win, 45% with a loss. JCC lose four starters to byes and are projected for 60.7. They also own Bullish's first-round pick, so a JCC win would pay twice.

What it means

The Central sends one team for sure, and maybe two. The winner in Hauk Tua's building is in good shape. The loser needs help. In the West, if Fully Cooked lose and Mailing It In win, Mailing take over first. And the two byes are up for grabs: Bullish and Fully Cooked hold them today, and both lose a lot of that grip with a loss.

See you after the games. Bring the coffee.

columns.title: Superflex is coming. Is your QB room ready?
columns.author: devin
columns.teaser: Superflex arrives in 2027, and with it a two-QB keeper limit. Who's loaded, who's squeezed, and why the defending champs should be nervous.
columns.caption: Fernando Mendoza, Son of Tinactin's first-round rookie on the taxi squad
columns.html:
Last August, this league bought seven quarterbacks at the auction for a combined $32. Patrick Mahomes went for $2. So did C.J. Stroud. The most anybody paid for a QB was $14, for Lamar Jackson. Kenneth Walker went for $66.

That market is about to disappear. In 2027 the lineup grows to nine starters, and the new one is a SuperFlex: QB, RB, WR or TE. Nobody is putting a running back there. Superflex turns this into a two-quarterback league, and quarterbacks score more than anybody else on the field.

We've been getting previews all season. Thirty-three times this year, a quarterback has scored 20 or more points on an FBP bench. The latest came in week 9, when Stroud put up 35.4 on Sour Grapes' bench. They started Dak Prescott, who scored 19.5. Under this year's rules there was nowhere to play him. Next year, that's a start.

What changes

  • Lineup: 1 QB, 2 RB, 2 WR, 1 TE, 1 FLEX, 1 SuperFlex, 1 DST. Rosters are 20 active, 3 IR and 5 taxi.
  • QB keeper limit: a team can keep two non-rookie QBs, plus any rookie QBs from that year's draft. A QB who spent his rookie year on the taxi squad can be kept into year two, but he takes one of the two spots.
  • Rookie QBs get pricier: rookie salaries now come from a formula based on where a player went in the NFL draft and where he goes in ours. The top price for a QB is $12, double the old top QB price of $6.

The math

Twelve teams starting two QBs is 24 starters, out of 32 NFL starting jobs. Add byes and injuries, and the 24th QB is often a backup. The average FBP starting QB this season has scored 18.6 a week. Rank the rostered QBs by points per game and the 12th-best is right around that number, at 18.4. The 24th is down at 13.2. So the gap between a team with two real starters and a team scrambling for its second one is real, and it shows up every single week.

That's why the keeper limit matters as much as the slot. Without it, the teams already hoarding quarterbacks would just keep all of them and starve everybody else. With it, the surplus has to go somewhere: traded, or thrown back into the auction.

Deadline day, Superflex edition

Today's NFL trade deadline gave us a small taste of how this works. Two FBP quarterbacks changed NFL teams in the last week, and both landed somewhere another FBP quarterback is hurt.

Hauk Tua's Kirk Cousins was traded to Minnesota today. The Vikings' starter, Kyler Murray, is week-to-week with a hamstring injury, and Murray belongs to Jesus Christ College. Last week, Mailing It In's Jacoby Brissett went to Baltimore, where he's expected to start Monday night with Lamar Jackson hurt again. Lamar belongs to the Fist of the Magi.

In a one-QB league, an injured starter's backup is a waiver-wire curiosity. In Superflex, he's a starter, and somebody else's bad news is your lineup.

The QB rooms, priced for 2027

Salaries below are what each QB costs next year after his escalator. Rookies who stay on the taxi squad all season keep this year's price. Points per game are this season through week 9, counting the games he played.

  • Son of Tinactin: Love $10 (20.6), Daniels $23 (19.2), Young $7 (18.3), Mendoza $6 (taxi rookie)
  • Bullish on da Bears: Purdy $10 (21.4), Williams $15 (18.4), Sanders $5, Beck $1 (taxi rookie)
  • MR. FROBOT: Burrow $20 (24.9), Shough $5 (18.2), Hurts $14 (16.0, IR), Simpson $3 (taxi rookie), Jones $3
  • Sour Grapes: Stroud $5 (20.5), Prescott $15 (18.6)
  • Hauk Tua: Maye $12 (19.9), Cousins $7 (19.1), Mayfield $4 (8.5), Allar $1 (taxi rookie)
  • The Fist of the Magi: Goff $12 (18.4), Jackson $17 (15.8 in five games), Penix $11 (13.7)
  • Hold Timers: Lawrence $11 (18.4), Nix $12 (14.5)
  • Thots & Players: Allen $30 (25.1), Ward $6 (12.6), McCarthy $6 (8.5)
  • Fully Cooked: Mahomes $5 (17.8), Darnold $4 (13.2, IR), Milton $6, Milroe $3
  • Wholey Club: Stafford $9 (15.9), Jones $4 (9.1)
  • Mailing It In: Lock $7 (15.6 in three games), Smith $20 (14.5), Brissett $3 (13.9), Herbert $10 (10.1)
  • Jesus Christ College: Willis $9 (13.1), Murray $9 (12.3), Dart $6 (IR), Richardson $3, Klubnik $3, Payton $3

Best suited

Son of Tinactin. One of the worst records in the league, and still the best quarterback room in it. Love, Daniels and Young are all starters, and Mendoza is a first-round rookie on the taxi squad. They can only keep two, which makes the others the most valuable trade chips in the league this offseason. And they hold two 1sts, projected 1.02 and 1.09. Take the top rookie QB on the board and he doesn't count against the limit in his first year.

Bullish on da Bears. The 1 seed has Purdy at 21.4 a game and Caleb Williams at 18.4, both 27 or younger next fall, and the pair costs $25 combined. Bullish don't have to do anything clever. They just keep both.

MR. FROBOT. Burrow is putting up 24.9 a game, second only to Josh Allen, and Tyler Shough has given them 18.2 a game for $2. He costs $5 next year. That leaves Jalen Hurts as a surplus. He's on IR right now, but at $14 he's a starter some other team will pay for.

Sour Grapes. Stroud at $5 is one of the best value contracts at the position, and week 9 showed it. Prescott turns 34 next season, but at $15 he's a fine second starter for a year or two. They also hold the projected 1.03 and $210 to spend, tied for the most in the league.

Worst prepared

Mailing It In. The defending champs are 5-3-1 and hold the 4 seed, and they've done it with the worst QB play in the league. Their starting QBs average 12.1 a week. They've gone shopping since: Drew Lock and Geno Smith are new. But Justin Herbert has given them 10.1 a game, Smith will be 36 at kickoff and costs $20 next year, and Brissett just took a job filling in for somebody else. Their 2027 1st belongs to Son of Tinactin. They need a starter, maybe two, and they'll be shopping in the most expensive QB market this league has ever had.

Jesus Christ College. Six quarterbacks, and the best of them is Malik Willis at 13.1 a game. Jaxson Dart is the long-term piece, but his season ended with a knee injury in week 2. Kyler Murray is hurt, and Minnesota just traded for Kirk Cousins. JCC hold the projected 1.05 and 1.12 and $205 to spend, so they're likely to come out of the rookie draft with a quarterback.

Wholey Club. Matthew Stafford is producing, but he'll be 39 at kickoff, and Daniel Jones has been a 9.1-a-game backup. The good news is they hold two 1sts, projected 1.01 and 1.11, and $210 to spend. A rookie QB at 1.01 is the obvious move.

On the fence: Thots have the league's best QB in Josh Allen, but he's $30 next year at 31, and the backups behind him, Cam Ward and J.J. McCarthy, have averaged 12.6 and 8.5. Fully Cooked lead the West with Mahomes at $5, but Sam Darnold is on IR and the rest of the room is Joe Milton and Jalen Milroe. Hauk Tua have Maye and Cousins scoring like starters, but Cousins turns 39 before next season and just changed teams. Fist of the Magi went from three starters for two spots to a $17 Lamar who has played five games, a Goff who scored 5.3 in week 9, and Michael Penix at 13.7. Hold Timers have Trevor Lawrence and a $12 Bo Nix who's put up 14.5 a game.

What to do now

If you have three starting QBs, you can sell one now, until the FBP trade deadline at noon Eastern on Thursday, December 3, just before week 13. Or you can sell in the offseason, between the start of the new league year and keeper day. Wait past keeper day and the third one goes back into the auction for nothing.

If you have one, start shopping now. Every team's second quarterback just became a starter, and the price of the 24th-best QB is about to go up a lot more than the price of the 12th.

And if you hold an early 1st, this rookie class has quarterbacks the mocks like: Drew Mestemaker, Darian Mensah, CJ Carr and Arch Manning all go in the first round of the NFL mocks. A rookie QB doesn't count against the two-QB limit in his draft year. In year two, he does.

columns.title: Rumor mill: a taxi-squad pass for rookie QBs?
columns.author: rex
columns.teaser: People around the league want a break for rookie quarterbacks who spend their first year on the taxi squad, and the league office might be listening. Plus a reminder on that seventh playoff spot.
columns.caption: Carson Beck, Bullish on da Bears' rookie QB on the taxi squad
columns.html:
You didn't hear it from me. But the Superflex keeper limit has people talking, and the talk has reached the league office.

Here's the rule as it stands for 2027. Each team can keep two veteran quarterbacks, plus any QB it drafts in that year's rookie draft. A rookie who spent his first season on the taxi squad can be kept into year two, but he takes one of the two spots.

Not everybody loves that last part.

What people are saying

One executive whose team is already up against the two-QB limit didn't hold back:

"In practice it means only rookies who are studs in year 1 will get kept and defeats the purpose of making them a draft commodity."

His point: if a second-year QB has to beat out a proven veteran for a keeper spot, nobody's keeping the kid who needs a year to develop. So why spend a pick on him in the first place?

A different source put the case for a fix in one line:

"It's another incentive to invest in developmental guys."

What's being floated

A rookie QB who spends his entire rookie season on the taxi squad would be exempt from the two-QB limit in year two. A team could keep him as a third quarterback alongside its two veterans. Promote him at any point during his rookie year and the exemption is gone.

There's a limit, too. The version I'm hearing about allows one exempt QB per team. Stash two or three rookie QBs on the taxi squad and only one of them gets the pass into the following year. Any others would have to win one of the two regular spots. Nobody gets to turn the taxi squad into a QB warehouse.

Nothing's on paper. Nothing's been decided. But the league office is listening.

Who it would help right now

Four teams have a rookie QB who has spent the whole season on the taxi squad so far:

  • Son of Tinactin: Fernando Mendoza, $6 next year
  • MR. FROBOT: Ty Simpson, $3
  • Hauk Tua: Drew Allar, $1
  • Bullish on da Bears: Carson Beck, $1

For three of them it's a cheap lottery ticket they wouldn't have to throw back. For Son of Tinactin it's real. They already have Jordan Love, Jayden Daniels and Bryce Young, and under today's rule Mendoza would be fighting all three for two spots. With the exemption, he's safe, and they only have to move one veteran.

There's a catch, and it's sitting in Las Vegas. Kirk Cousins was traded out of town today. If Mendoza starts getting snaps for the Raiders, Son of Tinactin has a choice: activate him and give up the exemption, or leave his points on the taxi squad and protect his spot for next year. Promote him and they also lose the frozen salary and the sixth-year option. From what I hear, the league office is fine with that trade-off. That's the deal: be patient with the kid, and you get to keep him.

Rex's take

I'm a draft-picks-are-lottery-tickets guy, and this rule makes the tickets worth buying. Superflex is going to make every quarterback expensive. Letting teams grow one of their own, as long as they actually wait on him, is a fair trade.

About that seventh playoff spot

Don't forget the other rumor. Word is still that the playoff field could grow to seven teams in 2027: three division winners, three wild cards on record, and a seventh seed off the all-play board, with only the 1 seed getting a bye.

Here's how it would look after week 9:

  1. Bullish on da Bears (bye)
  2. Fully Cooked vs. 7. Thots & Players
  3. MR. FROBOT vs. 6. Hold Timers
  4. Mailing It In vs. 5. Hauk Tua

Hold Timers get in on record as the third wild card, and Thots take the all-play spot. The team that would feel it most is Fully Cooked: the 2 seed is a week off today, and under the new setup it's a home game.

If you've got an opinion on either one, take it to the commissioner. I'm just telling you what I hear.

columns.title: The best franchise wakes up, the worst one is in first, and the East is the FBP Least
columns.author: sal
columns.teaser: MR. FROBOT win a third straight and take the Central, Fully Cooked sit alone atop the West later in a season than they ever have, and Bullish on da Bears open a three-game lead on the rest of the East.
columns.caption: Joe Burrow, MR. FROBOT's red-hot quarterback
columns.html:
It's a tale of two franchises. The most successful franchise in league history is back where it usually is. The team with the worst record since this league went PPR is in first place. If you had both of those on your card in September, you're lying.

FROBOT are back

MR. FROBOT started 2-4. They're now leading the Central. Three straight wins: 139.3, 153.4 and 151.6 this week, the top score in the league. That's 148 a game over three weeks. They have the most points in the league (1,192.7), the No. 1 power ranking, and the 3 seed. Three teams are 5-4 in the Central. FROBOT hold the tiebreak on total points, and it isn't close.

None of this should surprise anyone. Go back to the league's first season in 2011 and nobody has won more. Sean's franchise has four titles (2012, 2014, 2016 and 2023) and six trips to the title game, both the most in league history. Since the switch to PPR in 2019, Mailing It In have more rings, two to FROBOT's one, but nobody wins more often week to week. FROBOT are 71-29-1 in that stretch, a .703 winning percentage and almost 90 points better than anybody else. They finished first in the regular season three times and went 13-1 in 2024. Last year's 8-5 counted as a down year for them. The slow start this year was the strange part. This is just them getting back to normal.

The engine is the Cincinnati stack. Joe Burrow has 39.5 and 29.5 the last two weeks. Tee Higgins added 20.2 this week. And CeeDee Lamb, who doesn't even play in Cincinnati, put up 33.5. The computer has FROBOT's playoff chances up from 88% to 96%, and their odds of winning the Central from 38% to 60%.

Fully Cooked, of all teams

Fully Cooked are 6-3 and alone in first place in the West. Read that twice. From 2019 through 2025, this franchise went 37-64. That's the worst record in the league over that stretch. They've never had a winning season in the PPR era; their best was 7-7 in 2024. They finished last in 2023, and they're one of three teams that haven't played in a title game since 2019.

I went back through the weekly standings as far as they go, to 2019. Fully Cooked have never been in first place by themselves this late in a season. The closest they came was 2022, when they were tied for the West lead after Week 9 and lost the tiebreak on points. The only other time they had first place to themselves was the Week 8 standings in 2019, and that was at 4-4.

This year they've earned it. Fully Cooked have the most all-play wins in the league at 72-26, meaning they'd have beaten everybody else that week in 72 of 98 tries. They're second in points. They hold the 2 seed, and the computer gives them a 61% chance at a bye and a 71% chance to win the division. Two more wins and they've clinched the first winning season in franchise history. Five games left. Next up is Thots & Players, and that game is close to a coin flip.

Welcome to the FBP Least

Bullish on da Bears are 7-2 and three games up on the rest of the East. I'd call it a division race, but there's nobody racing. Wholey Club, Son of Tinactin and Jesus Christ College are a combined 9-17-1. Bullish are 3-0 against them, and the computer has them at 99.5% to win the division.

They're still not a great team on paper. Bullish are seventh in points and have a losing all-play record (48-50). But Ja'Marr Chase has put up 31.1 and 31.5 in his first two weeks, and Bullish have scored 146.8 and 146.7 since he showed up. They walked into Thots' building as a 2-to-1 underdog this week and won by 35.

The games

MR. FROBOT 151.6, Son of Tinactin 83.3

Lamb 33.5, Burrow 29.5, Javonte Williams 22.4, Higgins 20.2. Jordan Love put up 36.2 for Son of Tinactin, and he got no help: nobody else on the team cracked 15. Tinactin also left Bryce Young's 20.3 on the bench.

Fully Cooked 146.7, Jesus Christ College 82.6

Kenneth Walker III scored 36.3, the most by any starter this week. Puka Nacua added 35.0. Between them, those two outscored JCC's top five starters combined. JCC are 2-7 and five games back in the East.

Bullish on da Bears 146.7, Thots & Players 111.2

Chase 31.5, Brock Purdy 25.3, Brock Bowers 22.3. Bullish even left Shedeur Sanders' 22.7 on the bench. Matthew Golden put up 32.4 for Thots, but Josh Allen gave them 12.9 and Tucker Kraft 1.9. That's three straight losses for Thots.

Hauk Tua 121.8, Mailing It In 103.3

In my preview I said Hauk Tua's season was on the line. They answered. Christian Watson scored 30.1 and the 49ers defense 23.0. Bijan Robinson put up 26.7 for the champs, but Jaxon Smith-Njigba was held to 12.1. Mailing have lost two straight and slipped from the 2 seed to the 4.

Sour Grapes 93.9, Hold Timers 82.5

Bucky Irving 28.5, Dak Prescott 19.5. Sour Grapes also left C.J. Stroud's 35.4 on the bench, again. Meanwhile Hold Timers sat the Chicago defense (20.0) and Travis Kelce (17.3) and started D'Andre Swift, who gave them 3.1. Their best possible lineup would have scored 110.3 and won. Instead they dropped out of the playoff picture.

Wholey Club 64.5, The Fist of the Magi 56.6

The lowest-scoring game of the year. Wholey Club's best player was the Jacksonville defense, again, with 15.0. The Magi got 0.0 from Ladd McConkey, who didn't play, and 0.5 from Josh Jacobs. Last week I said that if the Magi couldn't beat Wholey Club, I'd stop calling them a contender. They couldn't. Four straight losses, and their playoff chances are down to 14%.

Awards watch

Rising:

  • CeeDee Lamb moved into the top three in the MVP race at 201.8, passing Josh Allen. Smith-Njigba still leads at 232.1, with Jahmyr Gibbs second at 209.2.
  • Puka Nacua, Ja'Marr Chase, Christian McCaffrey and Javonte Williams all moved onto the All-FBP second team.
  • Patrick Mahomes is closing in on Best Value. At $2 he's at 71.0 points per dollar, behind only Deebo Samuel's 74.6.
  • C.J. Stroud has 164.1 points on Sour Grapes' bench. Nobody will catch him for Left on the Bench.

Falling:

  • Hold Timers lost both of their second-teamers. D'Andre Swift and Amon-Ra St. Brown are off the All-FBP list.
  • Kyren Williams and Jonathan Taylor also dropped off the second team.
  • Josh Allen still has the first-team QB spot, but 12.9 this week dropped him out of the top three for MVP.

Fully Cooked now have three All-FBP players: Walker and Trey McBride on the first team, Nacua on the second.

Next week

columns.title: The 1 seed is the underdog, and the champs have to hold off Hauk Tua
columns.author: sal
columns.teaser: Hauk Tua visits Mailing It In with their season on the line, Bullish walks into Thots' building as a 2-to-1 underdog, and the Magi get the one team that has their number.
columns.html:
Last week I told you the West was fine. Then the West went 0-4. So take this with whatever you take your coffee with: halfway through the season, eight teams have a real shot at six playoff spots, and four of them live in the Central, all within a game of each other.

This week the 1 seed plays a road game it's expected to lose, the defending champs get a team that has nothing to lose, and the Magi get the league's lowest scorer, which happens to be the one team that's beaten them six times. Let's go to the board.

The matchups

Win chances come from the site's computer, which plays out the rest of the season 20,000 times. Series records count every meeting since 2019, playoffs included.

Hauk Tua (4-4) at Mailing It In (5-2-1) — game of the week

No game on the slate moves more playoff odds. Hauk Tua sit at 42% and can go to 58% with a win or 29% with a loss. That's a 28-point swing on one Sunday. Mailing goes to 93% with a win and 74% with a loss.

The computer has Mailing a 55% favorite, about as close to a coin flip as it gets. The series is 4-4, but Mailing has won the last three, including a round-one playoff game in 2024 by 55. Hauk Tua put up 153.6 last week, the best score in the league, and left 28.2 from Kirk Cousins on the bench while they did it. The champs just lost on Monday night by 3.6. If you're picking an upset, this is where I'd look.

Bullish on da Bears (6-2) at Thots & Players (4-4)

The 1 seed is a 2-to-1 underdog. Thots are a 67% favorite, and I understand why: 1,022.3 points, second in the league, and an all-play record of 58-30. Bullish are eighth in points at 853.3, with an all-play record of 39-49. Eight weeks in, the computer still doesn't believe in them.

But Bullish just scored 146.8 with Ja'Marr Chase in the lineup, and they're 95% to make the playoffs either way. What they're playing for is the bye: 61% with a win, 27% with a loss. Thots are playing for their footing. They've lost two straight, and a loss drops them to 72% to make it and 4% for a bye. These two have met three times in the playoffs. Thots lead the series 6-5.

Wholey Club (3-5) at The Fist of the Magi (4-4)

The Magi are a 72% favorite, and they need every bit of it. Three straight losses took them from first in the Central to last, and they've averaged 77.7 over that stretch. Win and they're back to 45%; lose and they're at 20%.

Here's the problem. Wholey Club owns this series 6-2 and has won the last two. Wholey is last in points, at 726.2, and averaging 79.7 over its last three, so neither team is scoring right now. Last week I said that if the Magi can't win this one, I'll stop calling them a contender. I'm not taking it back.

Hold Timers (5-3) at Sour Grapes (2-6)

The new Central leader is a 67% favorite and has won three straight, averaging 128.9 in that stretch. Hold Timers lead the series 5-3. A win puts them at 77% to make the playoffs and 38% for a bye. A loss drops them to 50%. In a division this tight, there's no such thing as a safe Sunday. Sour Grapes are at 0.2%, and this is mostly about pride.

Son of Tinactin (3-4-1) at MR. FROBOT (4-4)

FROBOT is the league's top scorer at 1,041.1, 131.0 a game over the last three, and an 80% favorite. They've beaten Son of Tinactin seven straight times and lead the series 8-1. A win puts them at 91% to make the playoffs; a loss, 76%. SOT is at 5%, 15% with a win.

Jesus Christ College (2-6) at Fully Cooked (5-3)

Fully Cooked is a 74% favorite, and nobody in the league has better bye odds, at 40.5%. That goes to 48% with a win and 21% with a loss. Their all-play record of 63-25 is the best in the league. JCC is coming off its second win of the year, and here's one for you: JCC leads this series 7-4.

  • Lowest bar: Wholey and the Magi have averaged a combined 157.4 points over their last three weeks. One of them wins Sunday anyway.

See you next week. Bring the coffee.
